headline: Vendor booths
lead: Food trucks, cooking booths, drinks, snacks, crafts, merchant booths, activity booths, nonprofit info tables for Elk Grove Lunar New Year Tết 2027.

meta.description: Apply for a vendor booth on Eventeny for Elk Grove Lunar New Year Tết 2027. See fees, spots left, and how selection works.

waitlist.title: Apply for single booth or an entire zone
waitlist.bodyAfter: Round 1 closed Nov 5. Round 1 decisions were around Nov 10.
waitlist.partnerIntro: Two ways to join the map: apply for a standard booth on Eventeny, or inquire about a named Custom Zones corner.

paths.title: Single booth on Eventeny
paths.body: Food, drinks, snacks, crafts, merchant, activity, and nonprofit info booths — apply through Eventeny.

paths.title: Custom Zones
paths.body: A named corner on the festival map — decorate it yourself or ask us to help bring your block to life.

cta.label: Apply on Eventeny
cta.note: Sign in or create a free Eventeny account. Most applicants pay a **$25** application deposit when they apply for a single booth. Nonprofit, community info, and free kids activity tables pay no deposit — and the free kids activity form does not ask for a credit card.

inventory.title: Booth inventory
inventory.editorNote: Staff/agent only — not rendered on eglny.com. **# of spots** and **Remaining** in inventory.table are author-set literals from Bao. Never derive them from caps, Round 1 fill, applicant counts, or formulas.
inventory.intro: Here’s how many booths we’re planning for, how many are still open, and what the weekend fee is. Ops / host / district pads are reserved separately and are not in these counts.

rows: Open food / on-site cooking (canopy, truck, or trailer)
Corporate, merchants, craft, and paid activities

notes: **Same food type:** We may limit how many booths sell the same food or snack so the festival has variety. We can’t list every limit yet — that gets clearer as applications come in. If more than one vendor wants a limited type, we rank applications and offer the booth in that order. If the first person doesn’t pay, the next person gets the offer.

**Total map:** About **143** guest-facing pads (Zones A/B, roundabouts, Pavilion walkway, Rotary Grove; includes cooking + truck pads). Ops / host pads sit outside that count. Snack booths count toward general-pad capacity.

fees.title: Fees and terms
fees.intro: Fees are for the whole weekend (Saturday and Sunday). Same prices as on Eventeny. There is no early-bird discount — applying early helps you get a decision sooner in Round 1.

sections.title: Application deposit
body: Food, merchant, craft, and corporate booths pay **$25** when you apply.
bullets: If we accept you → the $25 counts toward your booth fee
If we don’t select you → we refund the $25

If we select you but you don’t pay by the deadline → you lose the $25, and we offer that booth **right away** to the next person on the selection waitlist for that booth type — not to Round 2 new applicants
If that happens in Round 1 → you move to the Round 2 waitlist without paying another deposit

sections.title: Nonprofit and kids tables
bullets: Nonprofit / community info: **no** application deposit; **$75** only if approved
Free kids activity (guests don’t pay): use the **Free kids activity tables** app — no fee, no card
Paid kids / guest activity → use **Merchant / craft / paid activity** ($150)

sections.title: Table and chairs
body: Paid vendor booths get **one standard table and two chairs**. Festival volunteers set them up before the weekend and take them down after.
bullets: **Tent / canopy is not included.** Bring your own if you want shade. It must be straight-leg, fit fully in your pad, and be weighted — no staking into asphalt.
**Free kids activity tables:** the festival provides furniture for kids programming (it may not be one table and two chairs).
Need more furniture? Bring your own.

sections.title: Locking your booth
body: An offer only holds until the pay-by date. **Paying the booth fee locks your spot** — cleanup deposits do not.
bullets: **Round 1 — cooking** (canopy, food truck, or trailer): pay **$375 of the $750** booth fee by **Fri, Nov 20, 2026** to lock. The rest of the booth fee (**$350** after your $25 deposit credit) plus cleanup deposits are due **Fri, Jan 29, 2027**, or you give up the booth.

**Round 1 — drinks:** pay **$250 of the $500** booth fee by **Fri, Nov 20, 2026** to lock. The rest of the booth fee (**$225** after your $25 deposit credit) plus cleanup deposits are due **Fri, Jan 29, 2027**, or you give up the booth.
**Round 1 — everyone else** (snack, merchant, corporate, nonprofit): pay the **full booth fee** by **Fri, Nov 20, 2026** to lock. Cleanup deposits are due **Fri, Jan 29, 2027**.
**Round 2:** pay the booth fee (and any deposits due) by **Fri, Jan 29, 2027** — or when you’re approved, if that’s later.

sections.title: Trash and cooking deposits
body: Food, merchant, and corporate booths also pay refundable cleanup deposits. They’re charged on **Fri, Jan 29, 2027** (or when you’re approved, if later). These deposits do **not** lock your booth.
bullets: **$100 trash** — every food, merchant, and corporate booth
**$500 cooking cleanup** — only if you cook on site (trucks/trailers, open flame, grills, fryers)
Pre-packaged / no-cook food → trash deposit only
after: You get the trash deposit back when you bag out and leave the space clean. You get the cooking cleanup deposit back if there’s no grease, oil, or burn marks.

sections.title: Temporary Food Facility (TFF) permit
body: If you sell food, drinks, snacks, or sealed take-home food, Sacramento County needs a Temporary Food Facility permit for the weekend. That fee is **separate** from the booth fee — we collect the County’s fee and pass it through at cost.
bullets: Already have a valid multi-event (MEV) or mobile food facility (MFF) permit that covers this event → send us your permit number; no TFF fee
Need a single-event TFF → we file with the County and charge their fee: **$116** for pre-packaged / low risk, or **$258** for food prep / high risk (County FY 2026–27 rates)
Charged after you’re approved, usually with the Jan 29 deposits

sections.title: Cancellations and refunds
body: Cancel by **Fri, Jan 29, 2027** → we refund booth fees you’ve paid, minus a **cancel fee of 25% of the booth fee (minimum $50)**. After that date, **no booth-fee refund** — the festival is already planned around your booth.
Elk Grove Park is our planned venue; permits are still in progress. If the festival can’t happen there, we refund deposits and booth fees in full (no cancel fee).
Weather: for each festival day that gets canceled, you get a **2028 credit** for half the booth fee — not cash. Only a venue cancellation is refunded in cash.

sections.title: Insurance (COI)
body: You do **not** need a certificate of insurance (COI) when you apply. Food booths, and any booth using electrical power or a generator, must upload a current general liability COI by **Fri, Jan 29, 2027** (same day as full booth payment and cleanup deposits) — or when you’re approved, if that’s later. Your booth isn’t fully confirmed until we review an acceptable COI.
bullets: **Who needs a COI:** every food booth on the Food app — including drinks, snacks, and sealed / prepackaged take-home food — plus any merchant, nonprofit, or kids booth that uses electrical power or a generator
**Who does not:** basic non-food booths with no power can confirm coverage in the vendor agreement (no COI upload)
**Coverage:** commercial general liability, occurrence form · **$1,000,000** each occurrence · **$2,000,000** general aggregate · must cover **Sat–Sun, Feb 13–14, 2027**

**Additional insured (list all three):** Cosumnes Community Services District, its officials, employees, agents, and authorized volunteers · Vietnamese American Community of Sacramento (VACOS) · Community Partners Advocate of Little Saigon Sacramento (cPALSs), as co-host
**Certificate holder:** Elk Grove Lunar New Year Tết 2027 / VACOS · 9950 Elk Grove-Florin Road, Elk Grove, CA 95624
after: You can upload a COI with your application if you already have one. Otherwise wait until closer to Jan 29. We’ll email accepted food and power vendors these guidelines again before the due date.

sections.title: Hours and load-in
bullets: Vendor hours: **11 AM–7 PM** Sat–Sun, Feb 13–14, 2027
Load-in: **Friday, Feb 12, 2027**
Tear-down: after 7 PM Sunday
after: Exact load-in and tear-down times come with your acceptance email.

timeline.title: How selection works
timeline.intro: We review applications in **two rounds**. Early applicants can lock a booth sooner. We also save some spots for strong later applications. The steps are the same in both rounds.

rounds.label: Round 1 — Closed
rounds.note: Most spots (~70–80%). Decisions around Nov 10. **Pay the booth fee by Nov 20 to lock your seat:** cooking booths pay **$375 of $750**; drinks pay **$250 of $500**; everyone else pays the full booth fee. Miss Nov 20 → that seat goes **right away** to the next Round 1 waitlisted vendor for that booth type; you lose the $25 deposit and move to the Round 2 waitlist (no new deposit). Cooking and drink vendors who locked still owe the rest of the booth fee plus cleanup deposits by Jan 29, or they give up the booth.

rounds.label: Round 2 — Open now
rounds.note: The seats we held back (~20–30%). Unpaid Round 1 seats are **not** thrown into this open pool — they go first to the Round 1 selection waitlist. Decisions around Jan 22 cover held-back seats and people still waiting (including unpaid Round 1 selectees). Pay by Jan 29. **Food and snack applicants:** wait until we publish the Round 1 food vendors and their menus before you apply. That list shows what’s already taken, so you can see if your type might waitlist — or whether you should apply with something different.

timeline.pathIntro: Everyone waits for a decision batch. Then one of these happens:

steps.title: Apply
steps.body: Submit on Eventeny with the $25 application deposit (required to be considered — nonprofit, community info, and kids activity tables pay no deposit). You don’t need insurance when you apply. Food booths and power/generator booths upload a COI later, by Fri, Jan 29, 2027, with full payment and deposits.

steps.title: Wait for selection
steps.body: We review everyone in that round together — not first-come, first-served. Food booths are ranked for how well the menu fits the festival. Other booths are reviewed for overall fit.

steps.title: One of three outcomes
steps.body: You’ll get one of these results.

outcomes.title: Offer sent
outcomes.body: You’re selected. Accept the offer (food vendors may get a recommended festival menu), then **pay by the deadline to lock your booth** (Round 1 cooking: $375 of $750 by Nov 20; drinks: $250 of $500 by Nov 20; everyone else: full booth fee by Nov 20).
outcomes.next: Once that payment clears, you’re on the map. Round 1 cooking and drink vendors still owe the rest of the booth fee plus cleanup deposits by Jan 29.

outcomes.title: Selection waitlist
outcomes.body: You’re next in line for that booth type. If a selected vendor misses the pay-by, we offer **that same seat to you right away** — we don’t hold it for Round 2 new applicants. **If you weren’t first pick for a limited food type,** you can stay on this waitlist for a possible promotion, **or** submit a new Round 2 application for a different food type that isn’t already taken. Separately: if **you** were selected in Round 1 and didn’t pay by Nov 20, you move to the Round 2 waitlist (no new deposit) and wait for Round 2 decisions around Jan 22.
outcomes.next: A waitlist spot is not a reserved booth until you get an offer and pay.

outcomes.title: Declined
outcomes.body: Not selected for this festival season. If you paid the $25 application deposit, we refund it.

steps.title: Pay → official vendor
steps.body: Your offer only lasts until the pay-by date. Pay on time and you’re on the map. **Miss Round 1’s Nov 20 booth-fee lock** and that seat goes to the next Round 1 waitlisted vendor right away; you lose the $25 deposit and join the **Round 2 waitlist** (no new deposit). **Round 1 cooking and drink vendors** who locked with the half booth fee but miss the **Jan 29** remainder + deposits **give up the booth** (same: next on the selection waitlist). Cancel by Jan 29 for a booth-fee refund minus the cancel fee; after that, no booth-fee refund.

timeline.footnote: Dates can shift a little if we need to. Spot counts by booth type were set with Round 1 decisions (around Nov 10).

criteria.title: Selection criteria
criteria.intro: We look at the whole round of applications together — not whoever paid first. Food applicants are ranked within their type. Craft, merchant, and info booths are reviewed for overall festival fit.
criteria.factorsIntro: For cooking and drink applicants, here’s roughly how much each factor counted in Round 1 and how much it counts in Round 2:

rows: Strong menu / festival fit — see [Food menu](/food-menu/) for examples
Worked with our festivals before (Elk Grove LNY / Great Lantern)
Can this booth succeed with our expected crowd size?
Clear specialty (focused menu, not everything under the sun)
Dietary and guest needs — see [Food menu](/food-menu/) for examples
Active food social media (real posts — not just a handle or follower count)

criteria.factorsNote: Round 1 used one blended “previous festival relationship and experience” line. Round 2 splits that into prior work with our festivals and other festival experience. If two applications score about the same, who paid the deposit earlier can break the tie. Local Elk Grove ties and cultural anchors can also matter a little.

restrictions.title: Restrictions
deny: Adult-oriented businesses or products — including tobacco, drugs, pornography, firearms, and dating services
Organizations that practice or promote discrimination in employment or services
restrictions.salesIntro: Even approved vendors may not display or sell:
sales: Firecrackers, fireworks, firearms, weapons, or other dangerous items
Vulgar, offensive, sexually explicit, or obscene materials
restrictions.footnote: We may ask you to remove any product or service that doesn’t fit a family festival. That call is final.
